en.title: $615,000 to Invest at 65: What an Annuity Pays vs. What a Dividend Portfolio Pays, Month by Month
en.desc: A fixed annuity promises a guaranteed paycheck but quietly loses ground to inflation every year, while a dividend portfolio starts lower yet can grow into something far larger. Before committing $615,000 either way, one comparison changes how both options look.

en.title: A 66-Year-Old Swapped QYLD for JEPQ in a $1.27 Million Portfolio. Here’s What Happened to His $8,467 Monthly Paycheck
en.desc: One retiree dumped a famous 12% yield fund for a rival that pays nearly the same, and the real difference has nothing to do with this month's check. The gap shows up years later, when inflation starts taking its cut.

en.title: Is a Bigger Monthly Check Costing You Your Nest Egg? JEPQ, KBWY and BND Put to the Test
en.desc: Three monthly payers provide paycheck-like income, but only one of them left the original investment standing in our test window. We tracked every distribution against the share price to see which checks came at the nest egg's expense.

en.title: Covered Call ETFs Pay Huge Yields. Here’s What Retirees Need to Know First.
en.desc: Four option-income funds promise fat monthly checks, but each one quietly takes something from you in return. Before you build a retirement paycheck around them, see what you surrender, and why a tax label can hide how much the fund actually earned.

en.title: How Much Does a 65-Year-Old Need in a Roth IRA to Collect $7,700 a Month Tax-Free Without Selling a Single Share?
en.desc: Traditional IRA withdrawals can quietly raise your Medicare premium and make more of your Social Security taxable. A Roth sidesteps both, but only if you build it to the right size and pick income funds that hold their payouts.

en.title: How Much Does a 66-Year-Old Need Invested to Collect $9,100 a Month Without Selling a Single Share?
en.desc: A six-fund and stock income ladder promises paychecks without ever selling a share, but one decision about Social Security can shrink the nest egg you need by hundreds of thousands. Which lever matters most, and which holding carries the biggest risk?

en.title: What Size Roth IRA Replaces a $135,000 Salary Tax-Free at 62?
en.desc: Your paycheck shrinks before it hits the bank, so replacing it dollar for dollar may mean saving far more than you need. See which target a 62-year-old retiree should actually chase, and why a six-fund income mix decides it.

en.title: What JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income (JEPQ) Sold: Marriott Leads on Monday
en.desc: The fund sold $247.7 million more than it bought, cutting 78 positions and adding to just four.

en.title: How a 69-Year-Old Collects $4,350 a Month From Just Three Tickers: SCHD, JEPQ, and VICI
en.desc: Retirement math usually demands a sprawling portfolio, but one retiree's three-ticker setup challenges that assumption by mixing yields so mismatched they almost seem designed to cancel each other out.
